channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Oil Gains as US Said to Consider Iran Strike Options
item.description: Oil rose after a report that the Trump administration asked the Pentagon to draw up strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections, and as a hurricane forced some US output to shut. Bloomberg's Stephen Stapczynski has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EU Striking Harder Line on China's Trade Gap
item.description: The European Union is striking a more assertive approach to China as the bloc's trade chief, Maros Sefcovic, heads into two days of negotiations in Beijing. The EU is preparing safeguards to limit imports of Chinese hybrid cars after their sales surged in Europe, which may be seen as an escalation. Bloomberg's Minmin Low and Oliver Crook break down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Issues Ethiopia Travel Advisory, Cites Long-Range Attacks
item.description: The US issued a security alert for Ethiopia, warning citizens to “reconsider” travel to the Horn of Africa nation due to the threat of long-range attacks as tensions with neighboring Eritrea escalate.
item.dc:creator: Fasika Tadesse

item.title: Le Pen Pushes Protege Aside to Assert Control Over Far Right
item.description: The uncomfortable partnership between Marine Le Pen and her protege Jordan Bardella at the top of France’s largest political party is becoming unstuck as the presidential campaign kicks into gear.
item.dc:creator: Samy Adghirni and Claudia Cohen

item.title: South Korea Rebukes Ukraine Over Claims of Helping Russia
item.description: South Korea urged Ukraine to stop making what it called “incorrect and inappropriate” allegations that South Korea was undermining sanctions against Moscow by helping alleviate Russia’s fuel shortages.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Trump Defends Border Policies in Texas as Senate Race Heats Up
item.description: President Donald Trump defended his immigration policies during a visit to Texas on Wednesday as he sought to boost struggling GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan and Joe Lovinger

item.title: TikTok Accused by NY of Running Secret Safety Tests on Teens
item.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James has added new allegations to a child safety lawsuit against TikTok Inc., accusing the platform of running secret experiments on teen users.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Carville and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Hegseth Is Performing Poorly, Sen. Tillis Says
item.description: US Senator Thom Tillis, a North Carolina Republican, says voting to confirm Pete Hegseth as the Secretary of Defense is one of his biggest regrets. He says Hegseth is performing poorly as an executive. Tillis speaks on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Israel Was Warned Before Oct. 7 Attacks: Reports
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, US Senator Thom Tillis, a North Carolina Republican, discusses the outlook for the Republican Party in the 2026 midterm elections. US Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, explains why he thinks the US should reexamine its relationship with Israel. Brett McGurk, former deputy assistant for national security affairs for the Middle East and North Africa and author of Brink: Inside the Race to Free the October 7th Hostages, says there can be no “political horizon or future” as long as Hamas maintains its claim to power in Gaza. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham’s Rise Complicates Green Leader’s Bid for UK Parliament
item.description: Green Party Leader Zack Polanski faces an uphill battle in his attempt to win a north London seat in the UK’s House of Commons on Thursday, as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham breathes fresh life into the governing Labour Party.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: Big Take: Texas Is Testing the Power of MAGA Inc.’s Money
item.description: An unpopular Republican Senate candidate in Texas created an opening for a Democratic challenger — and now Trump is playing “red line defense. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UPS Worker Missed Email, Letting China Get F-35 Parts
item.description: China managed to get a hold of parts from an F-35 stealth fighter jet after a UPS employee missed an email warning not to route the shipment through Hong Kong. Wendy Benjaminson reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: McGurk: No Political Future in Gaza While Hamas Remains in Power
item.description: Brett McGurk, former deputy assistant for national security affairs for the Middle East and North Africa and author of Brink: Inside the Race to Free the October 7th Hostages, says there can be no “political horizon or future” as long as Hamas maintains its claim to power in Gaza, while Israel’s narrow right-wing coalition leaves the government with little room to maneuver. McGurk also recounts the difficult hostage negotiations, rejects claims that Hamas was prepared to quickly release the captives after the attack and discusses the regional diplomacy underway with Saudi Arabia and the Palestinian Authority before October 7. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Senator Coons Says US Should Reexamine Ties With Israel
item.description: US Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, explains why he thinks the US should reexamine its relationship with Israel. Speaking on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition," Senator Coons also weighs in on the Iran conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Fed Minutes & Oil Flows (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A record-breaking run in stocks hit a wall as still-elevated oil prices stoked concerns that potential inflationary pressures could trigger Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes. Those worries sent the S&P 500 down from an all-time high. Brent crude fluctuated around $100 as traders weighed a pickup in Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz against resilient Middle East flows. Ten-year Treasuries bounced from session lows after a solid $39 billion sale, but yields remained near the highest since 2002.
On today's episode: Jeff Rosenberg, Managing Director & Portfolio Manager, Systematic Multi-Strategy Fund at BlackRock Jennifer Welch, Senior Geoeconomics Analyst for Bloomberg Economics Ed Ludlow, Host of Bloomberg Tech Dr. Amesh Adalja, Senior Scholar at Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s New AI Czar to Visit Top AI Firms on Silicon Valley Tour
item.description: Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence and newly named leader of President Donald Trump’s so-called Super Intelligence Force, is starting off his latest role with a trip to Silicon Valley for meetings with some of the AI industry’s most powerful executives.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Stocks Retreat From Records as Oil & Yields Stay Elevated
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Glenmede Chief of Investment Strategy and Research Jason Pride, Nuveen Head of Fixed Income Tony Rodriguez, Citi Senior Equity Research Analyst Ari Rosa, QTS Co-CEO Tag Greason, Raymond James Global Head, Private Capital Advisory Sunaina Haldea, Needham Senior Research Analyst John Todaro, Genesys Chairman & CEO Tony Bates, JLL Hotels & Hospitality, Americas CEO Kevin Davis, & HGTV Host & Author Tarek El Moussa. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Sued by Democratic Party Over Taxpayer-Funded TV Ads
item.description: The Democratic National Committee filed a lawsuit accusing the Trump administration of unlawfully using government money to pay for advertisements lauding the president that have been airing on cable and broadcast television stations across the US in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Houthi Attacks Kill Three at Saudi Airports, Including in Riyadh
item.description: The Iran-backed Houthis struck two airports in Saudi Arabia, killing three people and injuring dozens as the militant group intensifies its attacks on the kingdom while fighting Saudi-backed forces in Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: Bolsonaro Secures Four Key Party Endorsements in Brazil Race
item.description: Brazil presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro won the backing of four center-right parties on Wednesday, a day after a former adversary endorsed him, bolstering his campaign ahead of a tight runoff.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Augusta Saraiva
